cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

mechanism: A confidently corrects a seating arrangement but preserves B authorship and limits the edit to persuade B to relinquish the pencil.
confusable: Unlike criticizing a plan, A seeks physical decision control; unlike secure authority A narrows the takeover to protect B willingness.
comparison: Authorship of a social arrangement differs from credit and physical control of a faulty hinge.
seedUse: Use D36-b exes/tables/hours/pencil and S02-a calling a negotiated edit the intended decision.
